messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to calculate the CI of P_a
messages.subject_clean: [distance-sampling] How to calculate the CI of P_a
messages.body_plain:
Dear Eric;

Many thanks for this help, it worked out perfectly.
Happy and successful 2025 for you and your relatives.

El martes, 31 de diciembre de 2024 a las 3:01:41 UTC-5, Eric Rexstad escribió:
> Eric
>
> Welcome to the list.
>
> The summaries of fitted model objects produce only two measures of precision in estimates of detection probability: standard error and coefficient of variation. If you want a third measure of precision, namely confidence intervals, you'll need to calculate those yourself.
>
> Here is a bit of code that performs the confidence interval computation based upon the assumption the confidence interval is approximately log-normally distributed (Sect 6.2.1 of Buckland et al (2015):
>
> library(Distance)
> data("wren_snapshot")
> cu <- convert_units("meter", NULL, "hectare")
> easy <- ds(wren_snapshot, key="hr", transect = "point", convert_units = cu)
> out <- summary(easy$ddf)
> # extract P_a and se from summary object
> P_a <- out$average.p
> P_a_se <- out$average.p.se <http://average.p.se>[1,1]
> P_a_cv <- P_a_se / P_a
> # assume degrees of freedom >30
> zed <- 1.96
> # use log-normal based confidence intervals
> C <- exp(zed*sqrt(log(1+P_a_cv^2)))
> ucb.log <- P_a * C
> lcb.log <- P_a / C
> print(paste("CI bounds for P_a", round(lcb.log,4), round(ucb.log,4)))
>
> If you have questions, let me know.
> From: distance...@googlegroups.com <distance...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Eric Enrique Flores De Gracia <sai...@gmail.com>
> Sent: 30 December 2024 18:43
> To: distance-sampling <distance...@googlegroups.com>
> Subject: [distance-sampling] How to calculate the CI of P_a
>
> I have run a point-distance sampling analyses with binned distances and could not find the way to calculate the confidence intervals for the probability detection function. I will appreciate any help.
>
> Regards
> Eric
>

messages.subject: Density Surface Modelling
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am currently working on a project to estimate ungulate distribution and density using camera traps. I have completed my distance sampling analysis and was hoping to produce a density surface model to visualize the distribution of ungulates in space. My plan was to follow the example of density surface modeling from distancesampling.com <http://distancesampling.com> (https://distancesampling.org/dsm/articles/lines_gomex/mexico-analysis.html) however, some of the packages required for this code are no longer on cran (rgdal, maptools). I tried to work around this by downloading the code onto my mac and installing the packages from source but kept running into the following error:
configure: error: gdal-config not found or not executable.
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘rgdal’
* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.4-arm64/Resources/library/rgdal’

Is there any other workarounds for getting this code to work? Or other examples to learn from?

Thank you in advance.

Best,
Annika

messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] Density Surface Modelling
messages.body_plain:
Annika

Welcome to the list. Sorry you're having difficulty with the density surface modelling vignette.

I rebuilt that vignette several months ago specifically to remove the dependence upon the deprecated "rgdal" package. I'm fairly confident the vignette to which you provide the link does not depend upon "rgdal". I had a quick glance at the code again and don't see where that dependence might exist; we would not have been able to build the vignette if that dependence still existed.  Please check again and perhaps we could communicate off list if needed to sort out your code.

If you are hoping to build spatial models from camera trap data, have a look at this paper
Delisle, Z. J., Miller, D. L., & Swihart, R. K. (2023). Modelling density surfaces of intraspecific classes using camera trap distance sampling. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 14, 1287–1298.  https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.14093
Those authors provide a walk-through analysis of a portion of their data in the Supporting Information. I think that code is likewise "rgdal-free."

messages.body_plain:
Hi, I have an issue with .dat folders becoming read-only and then not being able to open them again after closing a project. It's also not possible to open the example projects due to the same reason. I've seen other people have had this issue but is there a fix?

I've tried to unmark the folders and use the attrib command line, but it doesn't remove the read-only status.

Would be grateful for any ideas. I'm using distance 8 on windows 10,  with projects saved within one drive. I can't change this set up as it's for a student practical.

thanks!

best wishes
Christian

messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] read only .dat folder issue
messages.body_plain:
Christian

Thanks for your report. Yes, the "read-only" .dat folder issue has been previously reported. The previous report traced the problem to files being backed up to Google Drive.  In your case, the files appear to reside on OneDrive and presumably are to be shared by students for their practical.

You don't mention whether the problem exists when the Distance project in question is not on OneDrive. I speculate the problem does not exist when OneDrive is taken out of the equation. I understand the practicality of using OneDrive for practicals, however, I think the prudent strategy would be to have the exported .zip files for the students to access from OneDrive. They would then save the Distance project to their local drive and carry out their analyses.

This side-steps having .dat folders on OneDrive that become read-only.

Let us know if this resolves your difficulties.

thanks a lot for your response. I can confirm now that it does seem to be a OneDrive issue - as a workaround I created a new project and saved it to the "Downloads" folder - which is not backed up by onedrive and I was able to save and reopen projects from here. Also, the error states that the folder is read-only but if I look at the properties of the project I created in downloads (which allows saving and opening) it is also read only. Maybe onedrive is changing some other attributes of the files as soon as it is saved in a one drive location? Are the sample projects available elsewhere as a download apart from inside the installation? They may work if I save them directly outside of onedrive.

Saving to 'downloads' will work for the moment, but won't allow students to save any projects outside of downloads (which isn't permanent) - so probably best on a usb drive if they need to be able to be able to use them elsewhere. I will encourage them to use R, but I did want to present the standalone software as an option too.

best wishes
Christian

messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] read only .dat folder issue
messages.body_plain:
Christian

Glad you've created a work-around. Similar to the previous user who noted their read-only problem arose from a folder marked for backup by Google Drive, you seem to have a similar situation with a location backed up by OneDrive. You may well be right that something is afoot with directory attributes with third-party backup solutions.

If you wish to make a copy of the Sample Project directory to a more handy location, you can access all files via the operating system here:

C:\Program Files (x86)\Distance 8\Sample Projects

You can then copy them to wherever you wish.

From: distance...@googlegroups.com <distance...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Christian <cdev...@gmail.com>

Sent: 23 January 2025 10:25
To: distance-sampling <distance...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] read only .dat folder issue

Hi Eric,

thanks a lot for your response. I can confirm now that it does seem to be a OneDrive issue - as a workaround I created a new project and saved it to the "Downloads" folder - which is not backed up by onedrive and I was able to save and reopen projects from here. However, if I copy sample projects from their default installation location (in Documents - also on OneDrive) to the "downloads" folder I still can't open them. Also, the error states that the folder is read-only but if I look at the properties of the project I created in downloads (which allows saving and opening) it is also read only. Maybe onedrive is changing some other attributes of the files as soon as it is saved in a one drive location? Are the sample projects available elsewhere as a download apart from inside the installation? They may work if I save them directly outside of onedrive.

Saving to 'downloads' will work for the moment, but won't allow students to save any projects outside of downloads (which isn't permanent) - so probably best on a usb drive if they need to be able to be able to use them elsewhere. I will encourage them to use R, but I did want to present the standalone software as an option too.

best wishes
Christian
